current.text: Dejounte Murray is locked into the starting lineup at guard, which limits Fears' lead guard role.

Fears and Herb Jones compete for the last starting spot next to Murray, Trey Murphy, Zion Williamson and likely Yves Missi. Reporting says Joe Dumars wants Fears in the lineup, and a Pelicans beat reporter thinks Fears will start over Jones.
Josh gives Fears at least a 50/50 chance to start and is moving him up his rankings. He would draft Fears only if Fears starts.
The Pelicans have a crowded rotation, with about eight players who could start. Fears has no clear 30-minute role yet.
Experts treat him as a late flyer with upside, taken from round 11 on in mock drafts. He would be clearly better with 30 or more minutes.
He is a handcuff to Dejounte Murray. If Murray is hurt or traded, Fears could give top 70 numbers.
He is a tier 8 point guard, and lasting to round 13 means he is badly under drafted.
New coach Jamahl Mosley brings a defense-first identity.
The Pelicans project as a weak team near the bottom of the West, at about 34 wins.

durable.text: He is a downhill lead guard who is dynamic with the ball. He keeps attacking the rim even when he is not scoring there, and he contributes across categories.
He is not a good enough three-point shooter to play off the ball as a two guard. He is slightly undersized and struggles on defense.

note: Fears is a 1 USD player on both sites (Yahoo rank 168, ESPN rank 129). He went undrafted in our league last season, so he sits right at the edge of our 144-player draft. That makes him a fine last-dollar flyer, especially for a manager who already has Dejounte Murray. His best category is steals and he adds some assists, but his FG% (43%) and turnovers hurt. He fits a build that already tolerates low FG% better than one that relies on FG%. Early on, check whether he starts over Herb Jones, whether he reaches 30 minutes and how healthy Murray is. If none of these break his way, he is waiver material.
